title: How FlexAI handles a request

nodes.label: Expo mobile app
nodes.note: Screens for auth, onboarding, workouts, coach, social and analytics. Axios API modules per domain, React Query for server state, Zustand stores for auth and the active workout.

nodes.label: Express middleware
nodes.note: app.ts: Helmet, CORS allow-list, gzip, express-rate-limit (off in dev), a request ID header, Morgan logging through Winston, then a central error handler.

nodes.label: Routers + controllers
nodes.note: 13 route modules under /api/v1. Most mount authenticate (JWT) and validate() (Zod schemas) before the controller calls a service.

nodes.label: Workout service
nodes.note: workout.service.ts: starts and completes workouts, logs sets, and on completion updates the user's streak and awards XP.

nodes.label: Workout generator (RAG)
nodes.note: WorkoutGenerationService: embeds the request, runs a vector search, prompts Gemini with only those exercises, then drops any exercise ID it was not given.

nodes.label: AI coach
nodes.note: CoachService: system prompt from the user's profile and recent workouts, last 10 messages as history, replies capped at 500 output tokens, both sides saved.

nodes.label: Gamification service
nodes.note: Fixed XP per action (workout 100, post 20, challenge completed 500), level-ups, daily streak tracking and achievement checks.

nodes.label: Social + leaderboards
nodes.note: Feed posts, comments, likes, follows and challenges. Leaderboards read and write Redis sorted sets keyed leaderboard:<type>.

nodes.label: Auth service
nodes.note: Register, login, access and refresh tokens, email OTP verification and password reset, plus Google ID-token sign-in in oauth.service.ts.

nodes.label: Notification service
nodes.note: Stores device tokens and the notification inbox, and sends push messages to a user's devices with firebase-admin.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.note: Prisma schema: users, sessions, exercises, workouts and sets, routines, body metrics, coach chats, social entities, achievements, notifications.

nodes.label: Exercise embeddings
nodes.note: pgvector column on exercises (768 dims), filled by prisma/seed-embeddings.ts and searched with the <=> cosine operator.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.note: ioredis client with retry backoff. Optional at startup. Compose runs it with a 512mb allkeys-lru cap.

nodes.label: Gemini API
nodes.note: gemini-embedding-001 for vectors and gemini-3-flash-preview for workout plans and coach replies.

nodes.label: Google sign-in
nodes.note: OAuth2Client.verifyIdToken from google-auth-library checks the ID token sent by the app.

nodes.label: SMTP server
nodes.note: email.service.ts sends verification and password-reset OTP emails through a configurable SMTP host.

nodes.label: Firebase Cloud Messaging
nodes.note: sendEachForMulticast delivers push notifications to the stored device tokens.

flow: The app calls POST /routines/generate with its JWT. Helmet, CORS and the rate limiter run first, then authenticate and Zod validation.
The generator embeds a short description of the goal, equipment and level with gemini-embedding-001.
A cosine-distance query over the pgvector column returns the 30 closest exercises.
Gemini receives only those exercises and their IDs and returns a warm-up, main block and cool-down as JSON.
Exercise IDs outside the retrieved set are dropped and the plan goes back to the app.
Secondary path: when the user finishes a workout, the workout service saves it, updates the streak and awards 100 XP through the gamification service.
Secondary path: sign-up writes the user to Postgres and emails an OTP over SMTP. Google sign-in verifies the ID token instead.
